- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ days), model underestimates upside; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility; if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.67/0.00), reduce forecast variance by 30–50%.
- When sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of downward bias to forecast horizon.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates mean reversion; if sentiment is mixed or neutral, add 1–3% upward bias to align with historical mean.
